summary: Added 52 adversarial tests across 5 new test files (composer-state, status-view, LessonComposer, AuthoredLessonPreview, route page). One real bug surfaced and fixed: the composer reducer's `reorder` helper did not bounds-check indices, so REORDER_PHASES with `fromIndex=-1` and `toIndex=0` would silently splice-move the last element to the front. All targeted, project, lint, and type-check gates pass with 175 tests green (123 pre-existing + 52 new).
nonblocking_findings: Bug: `reorder<T>(arr, from, to)` in apps/integrated-math-3/lib/teacher/content-authoring/composer-state.ts did not bounds-check indices; `Array.prototype.splice` accepts negative or out-of-range values and silently mutates the array (e.g. `splice(-1, 1)` removes the last element). A stale UI passing out-of-range indices could scramble the phase/section/activity tree. Fixed in this pass by adding a defensive no-op for non-integer / negative / out-of-bounds from/to indices, so the rest of the reducer never sees a half-shifted array. The fix is covered by `composer-state-adversarial.test.ts: REORDER_PHASES with an out-of-bounds fromIndex is a safe no-op` and `REORDER_PHASES with an out-of-bounds toIndex is a safe no-op`.

Documentation: the JSDoc banner in `LessonComposer.tsx` and `AuthoredLessonPreview.tsx` references `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` to declare the safety property. A naive substring guard `expect(source).not.toContain('dangerouslySetInnerHTML')` would false-positive on these banners. The adversarial test `LessonComposer source does NOT use dangerouslySetInnerHTML for any authored text` strips block + line comments before matching `dangerouslySetInnerHTML\s*=` so it only catches actual JSX prop usage.

Pre-existing aggregate failures: the app-wide aggregate `npx vitest run apps/integrated-math-3` shows the same 9 pre-existing test-file failures documented in plan.md (objectiveProficiency, schema-blueprint, schema-vany-audit, ActivityRenderer-graphing-explorer, practice-blueprint, problem-families-modules-6-9, etc.). The new adversarial tests do not contribute to that count and run entirely green in the targeted Phase 3 gate.
